overall: The AG found the working group behind the March 13 letter was not a public body under the Open Meeting Law, and that two Charter and Rules Committee members did not deliberate outside a posted meeting. Complaint resolved, no violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a working group of council members, the mayor, and staff was a public body that had to comply with the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the working group fails the second prong of the public body analysis where it was not empowered to act collectively.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the working group failed to post meeting notices, hold open meetings, and create and maintain minutes.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the working group was not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged two councilors who sat on the Charter and Rules Committee, a quorum, deliberated outside a posted meeting through their work on the working group.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the information before us, we find that Ms. Murphy-Romboletti and Ms. Magrath-Smith did not deliberate outside of a posted meeting regarding the Municipal Finance Modernization Act and related topics.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
